title: A third fly connectome (male CNS v1.0) repeats the head-direction ring wiring of hemibrain and FlyWire and holds model bumps that 40 shuffles do not; its type-level wiring is closer to FlyWire
abstract: Question: two earlier SCI studies (sci a9ace630, sci 27a99efd) found ring-attractor wiring and bump-holding rate models in the fly head-direction circuit of two female connectomes, hemibrain v1.2 (FIB-SEM) and FlyWire v783 (TEM). Do these results hold in a third animal, the male CNS v1.0 (FIB-SEM, same FlyEM pipeline as hemibrain)? Where hemibrain and FlyWire differ, does the male CNS agree with hemibrain (a pipeline effect) or not? Approach: we applied the published code without change of method to 156 male CNS neurons (EPG, EPGt, PEG, PEN_a, PEN_b, Delta7, P6-8P9) and 143,125 synapses among them. Results: angles from EB-only wiring agreed with PB glomerulus labels (median EPG error 5.2 and 5.6 degrees). The EPG -> Delta7 -> EPG weight was a cosine with its peak at 180 degrees (R2 0.985; hemibrain 178, FlyWire 176). PEN outputs shifted by +51 degrees (left PB) and -48 to -57 degrees (right PB); all 40 PENs with data had the sign of their side; PEG shifts were near 0. The linear ring-mode pair was nearly degenerate (split 0.46%, a complex pair 0.631 +- 0.0014i; hemibrain 2.4%, FlyWire 4.2%). With label angles, random placement of the neuron-level variation gave larger splits (p = 0.006 with 8 angle bins, 0.042 with 16); hemibrain gave p = 0.28 to 0.39. After class-gain tuning, measured male CNS wiring held a bump (best score 0.94, 4 of 4 seeds); none of 40 type-preserving shuffles did (rank p = 1/41). A uniform two-gain model failed (0.06; hemibrain 0.73, FlyWire 0.65). Bumps locked to 5 to 11 stable headings, not to a continuous ring. One of 4 joint-tuned models turned the bump, in the predicted direction, in a narrow drive window. FlyWire-tuned gains held male CNS bumps in 4 of 4 seeds, hemibrain-tuned gains in 2 of 4. In 40 strong type-to-type input fractions, the male CNS was closer to FlyWire (median |log2| 0.30) than to hemibrain (0.42; bootstrap 89% of resamples). In 8 of 10 blocks where hemibrain and FlyWire differ twofold or more, mostly Delta7 -> PEN and PEG, the male CNS was closer to FlyWire. Thus a shared pipeline does not explain these differences. Limitations: one animal per connectome; simple rate model; no activity data; the near-degeneracy test is significant in one animal only and depends on binning.

display.caption: Ring wiring in three fly connectomes (HB hemibrain v1.2, FW FlyWire v783, MCNS male CNS v1.0). A: two-step EPG -> Delta7 -> EPG weight in the PB against EB angle difference (16 bins, divided by the mean); all three peak opposite the source. B: EB output angle minus PB input angle for each PEN and PEG neuron (dots) with circular means (bars). C: in the male CNS, angles from EB-only wiring agree with PB glomerulus label angles for EPG and PEG; PEN neurons sit about 55 degrees off, as their output shift predicts. D: EPG -> PEN synapses in the PB per PEN neuron; counts depend on the dataset.

Connectome-constrained rate model (code of sci 27a99efd). HB and FW values are the published ones; MCNS values are new. A: best persistence score after class-gain tuning for measured wiring (4 seeds) and type-preserving block and entry shuffles (MCNS: 20 + 20; HB, FW: 10 + 10); dashed line: best uniform two-gain model. B: number of stable headings reached from 64 cue headings. C: bump rotation speed against asymmetric PEN drive for all real models. D: gains tuned on one connectome and tested on another; cell text: median persistence score and number of seeds with score > 0.5.

Type-to-type input fractions (synapses from the source type divided by all input synapses of the target type) for 40 strong blocks. A, B: male CNS against hemibrain and against FlyWire (log axes; magenta: blocks where hemibrain and FlyWire differ at least twofold). C: for these 10 blocks, log2 fraction relative to hemibrain; the male CNS (diamonds) is closer to FlyWire in 8 of 10.

citations.reason: Source of the ring-wiring analysis code (angles, PB check, PEN shift, Delta7 profile, linear spectrum). We repeat its tests in a third connectome and confirm its main results.
Source of the rate-model code, the hemibrain and FlyWire extraction code and the published hemibrain and FlyWire rate-model results that we compare with.
